notes.title: v1.0.5 Marking Upgrade
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/daa7ef99e68155493f72ecdc566fa8f3c3bf5e66.png[/img]

I've given the marking features some love in this small update. This includes changes to how the pencils and chalk work, and how they work in conjunction with straight edges like the framing squares and the speed square.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/8a93dd8aec1000e6a50989b89cf7242dc134e299.png[/img]

First, there are no longer two methods of using the pencil. Please read the updated Marking instructions in the manual.

The procedure to use the pencil now is: 

[olist]
[*] place the pencil tip near wood
[*] touch the pencil to the wood to mark
[*] press and hold the ‘interact’ button to snap the pencil to a framing square or speed square edge to strike a straight line
[/olist]

Instead of the pencil automatically snapping to the straight edges like in previous versions, the player now has the choice to snap to the straight edge. This makes it easy to strike tick marks at measurements.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/9b831ccdf3eab09f0007ad6da9fff6be76bf8692.png[/img]

The same procedure can be used with the chalk and straight edges on the chalkboard.

In addition to the ability to transition from straight edge to freehand drawing, you can now use straight edges at oblique angles instead of them being required to be parallel to the marking surface. Give it a try and let me know what you think!

Have fun. Be productive.

- wooden robot

notes.title: Patch: Error handling
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/b85ce18cc582d8cc2b822e66416112bfe19aa16a.png[/img]

This patch adds better error handling in the event that a failure happens during saving or loading of important game data.

These errors can happen due to a variety of causes, the most extreme would be system failure during read/write operations, with the most minor being caused by exiting the game while saving/loading, or blocking saving/loading by having a file open while the game is trying to access it. 

If you happen to have an issue, the game will start in a safe mode and provide some instructions on how to try to fix the error.

I've made a significant effort to wrap all read/write operations with safety checks, and provided an error log to help debug the problem. If you cannot get back up and running, please reach out and I will do my best to help you.

If there is an error log, a timestamped file will be placed in the directory: [YOUR_WINDOWS_USER_PATH]/AppData/LocalLow/ScopatGames/vrkshop/ErrorLogs/

Have fun. Be productive.

- wooden robot

tags.feature: This patch adds better error handling in the event that a failure happens during saving or loading of important game data.

notes.title: vrkshop v1.0 Released!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/d755c6597bfc0723bb15756ee9244bcec531a1e9.png[/img]

vrkshop has now been officially released from Steam Early Access! 

The past year and a half I have been working with players to add new features and tweak existing features for vrkshop, and now, I feel good about transitioning out of Early Access. Thank you for all of the community feedback, positive and negative. It has helped shape what I am proud to claim is a unique VR experience.

The Early Access exit doesn't mean that development of vrkshop will stop, or that there are no bugs, or there is nothing left to tweak. It means that I feel that vrkshop finally brings together a solid core of woodworking capabilities, and that players can effectively bring their ideas to life and share those creations with others.

[h2]Update features:[/h2]
[list]
[*]Two new Free Play environments were added, and the main menu scene slide projector slides have been rearranged.
[*]Hand filtering was added to remove micro-jitter from your physical hand shake or hardware tracking errors.
[*]Added a seated-play option for players that primarily play seated in real life and work mostly at the in-game workbench. This will automatically require the remote-grab option to be enabled so you can pick items up from the floor, but there are still obvious limitations in this mode with respect to building large items near the in-game floor.
[*]The alarm clock in the workspaces now show your local time, with the alarm hand referencing the time you entered the scene.
[*]Simplified the interaction with the pegboard hooks. To remove them from the pegboard, use the -auxiliary- action (Y/B on oculus touch, or double tap the touchpad for vive). To reattach, hold near the pegboard and press either -auxiliary- or -interact-. 
[*]Steam achievements have been added.
[/list]

If you run into any problems, or have any suggestions, please reach out on the Steam Community forums, or the official [url=https://discord.gg/8zp6v5D]Discord server[/url].

Have fun. Be productive.

- wooden robot

notes.title: Update 14

[h2]The cloner tool has arrived![/h2]

The new cloner tool allows you to:

1. Quickly make copies of components for easy duplication
2. Reuse components across multiple Free Play levels
3. Share components with other players, and make use of other players' projects via the Steam Workshop

Use the new cloner tool to scan and then immediately build a copy or save projects for later in your Project Library. Once inside your Library, you can export these projects to Steam Workshop for others to use, or export them to a local .obj file to use in 3D modeling software.

notes.title: Update 13: Quality of Life Improvements
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/8ba702aa2955840f6c84f50f97020cb310596820.png[/img]

Today's update bring a few quality of life improvements!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/411ba4250a7ba5adae0c177d9c9dff67fc737c15.png[/img]

Check out the second page of the options menu to adjust the render scale and anti-aliasing to improve visual clarity at the expense of performance

[h3]Other improvements:[/h3]

- Saving times are dramatically improved

- Saved file size is significantly smaller

- A logo appears while saving instead of a black screen

- Smooth locomotion is much smoother across bumpy terrain

- Fixed a bug related to the player hands becoming jittery after a teleport while smooth locomoting

- Grabbing items within a very short range (3cm) now grabs in place and no longer snaps the item to the center point of the hand. Items outside of the short range but within grabbing range still snap to the hand. This improves fine adjustment grabbing.

- Small items like pencils, chalk, and nails snap firmly into grip and no longer flop around into the hand


If you have any feedback or problems with the update, please let me know in the Steam Community forums or on the official [url=https://discord.gg/8zp6v5D]Discord[/url]

Stay tuned for the next update.

Have fun. Be productive.

notes.title: Update 10: Miter Box, Scrap Cart, & Backup Save
notes.content:
[h1]Update 10 has arrived![/h1]

[h3]*NEW TOOL* Miter Box[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/254722d4c6b89b8b5e75decdacc6381a741894ed.png[/img]

A new tool has arrived to help you make straight, square cuts. Clamp one of the two provided miter boxes into the table vise, line a board up on top, place the saw into the slot, and cut as normal.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/d3f0c826275aeae2e943831bc83f893362f325fa.png[/img]

30, 45, 60, and 90 degree square slots, and a 45 degree off-vertical slot are provided.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/4325da6519a35035cd1021b871c15bb80e8ef6fb.png[/img]

The miter box can be used with or without the table vise.

[h3]Scrap Cart[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/837ba39300d59c19490c6c20ef62a316247263f3.png[/img]

The scrap cart provides a better way to destroy your extra parts. Simply place what you don't want inside the barrel, or directly on the cart. Lift the button shield and press the button to destroy everything within the bounds of the cart.

[h3]Backup Save[/h3]

notes.title: Update 9.1
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/093aaf22ec27a28074da054886dde6e5ce7121c4.png[/img]

This small update brings performance enhancements and gameplay bug fixes that I have been meaning to buckle down and sort out for a long time. 

[h3]Gameplay fixes: [/h3]

- Fixed bug with sawing multiple lumber. The saw now behaves more consistently when sawing through multiple lumber within the same lumber assembly and when sawing stacks of loose lumber.

- Large lumber assemblies no longer jump/hop when new lumber is nailed or when a member lumber is sawed

- Fixed mass calculation bug for certain orientations when sawing on a lumber assembly. This caused assemblies to lose their mass and seem very squishy. This no longer happens.

- Added consideration to the center of mass when computing the stiffness and damping properties of hand grips. This makes large, lightweight items not be as springy while holding them. (e.g. 5 boards strung together in a single line).

- Fixed a bug with the table vise so it grabs items more reliably on the first try.

- Fixed bug with manipulating lumber assemblies while they are held in the table vise, and then the table vise releasing the assemblies. This no longer happens.


[h3]Increased performance: [/h3]

- Changed from multi pass to single pass stereo rendering

- Using more shared materials to reduce draw calls

- Combined static meshes on main menu scene

- Ensured small meshes using same materials are being dynamically batched (e.g. primarily nails and lumber)

- Added Level of Detail to nails. They render more simplified or get culled as they are further away from you to save rendering time.

-----------------------------------

Check it out and be sure to leave comments in the [url=https://discord.gg/8zp6v5D]Discord server[/url] or Steam Community Forums.

Have fun. Be productive.

notes.title: Update 5: Getting Physical (and more)
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/a099ba663182e2300b4e75cec3505b97072b60de.png[/img]

The purpose of this update was to address a lot of the physics related issues that I've received feedback on over the initial weeks of vrkshop being available on Early Access. I've tried my best to take in, digest, and offer an incremental step towards more stable and predictable interactions, without giving up too much of the physical world.

As always, tell me what is working for you or what needs more attention. Thank you to those who have provided detailed descriptions of issues!

[h2]What is in the update?[/h2]

[h3]More present physical 'hands'[/h3]

The 'hands' no longer pass through the static objects in the room. Previously, your hand indicators tracked with your controllers fairly reliably. This caused a lot of problems with giving your hands god-like strength. 

A major benefit to this new behavior is that you can no longer punch your hands into the wall, and then grab the saw, causing it to jump into the netherworld between the vrkshop and the horrors of the outer-vrkshop. This is a mechanism I overlooked, well, simply because I developed the game and didn't realize people would do that.

[h3]-grab lock- replaces -pickup- action[/h3]

The -pickup- action has been replaced with -grab lock-. Aside from sounding more specific, the -grab lock- action works different from the plain -grab- when used on the SAW and the HAMMER. 

Using the plain -grab- action will grab the saw or hammer in the orientation that it is lying in, and not flip the tool around to the preset grab orientation.

-grab lock- will snap the SAW or HAMMER to the predefined grab orientation for those tools. Of course, -grab lock- still allows you to lock any other item to your grip like before.

This give you a little more flexibility with holding these tools, and hopefully further prevents the rage inducing scattering of your project across the room when all you were trying to do was move the hammer.

[h3]Other various changes:[/h3]

[olist][*] Added dynamic physics joint parameters based on an object's mass. This addresses the overly droopy and swingy heavy object grab behavior.

[*] Hands can now interact with the clipboard and calculator, no longer requiring the use of a pencil

[*] Modified workbench colliders to attempt to fix the ghost sliding of lumber

[*] Reduced the player grab distance to 0.15m to reduce inadvertent grabbing of stuff.

[*] Fixed a bug with respect to the grabbing of a nail or pill causing the loss of grab functionality of the hand.

[*] Added a 'no hand' icon warning instead of the 'x' when the player tries to saw a board while holding it, or tries to interrupt a sawing action by grabbing the item

[*] When a nail box is empty, it can now be discarded, or will be discarded on the next loading of a saved game, tidying up your vrkshop

[*] Added some margin on the smooth locomotion so the player no longer "plummets into the dirt through a 2mm gap in my 2x6 scaffolding"

[*] Added a player and item respawn feature if the player or items go outside of the play area.

[*] Added snacks to the free play material order form for Twash
[/olist]

And I'm sure I've added a few bugs in there along the way, so be sure to report those in the Community Forums.

Have fun. Be productive.

[h2]Don't lose your lunch - Smooth Locomotion is here![/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/d623ca37bd0fc99380da82d13b0994be02b0e626.png[/img]

Smooth locomotion is now an option that can be toggled on the clipboard options. Movement and rotation options can be toggled separately.

There are two types of smooth movement:

LOOK DIRECTION: Hold both the left-hand and right-hand teleport buttons down to move in the direction you are looking.

FREE MOVEMENT (Twin stick): Use the left joystick for forward/back & side strafing, and the right joystick for smooth rotation.

Note for Vive users: 
Vive controllers [b]only[/b] have the first option (look movement) available in the default SteamVR controller bindings. You can manually override by providing a binding to the 'move' and 'rotate' actions. These will work on the touchpads, but are incredibly sensitive.

notes.title: Update 2: A Grabbing and Physics Update
notes.content:
[h2]Update 2: A Grabbing and Physics Update[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/cafbdded927aabbcfd7421b26be1cee85ac53b7e.png[/img]

In this update I've started to address some of the issues around grabbing items and the physics joints and inter-item interaction.

Here is a list of things addressed:

1. The fixed-hold orientation items (the saw and hammer most noticeably) no longer snap to their rotation, but instead attempt to smoothly interpolate to the final rotation. You should notice a lot fewer items flying around your vrkshop (at least unintended items flying around your vrkshop).

2. You can now transfer items from one hand to the other with both -grab- and -pickup- (hold-lock) actions. This makes it easier to inspect items without dropping and re-picking them up. 

Note: While I'm on this topic, this is a reminder that if an item is 'stuck' to your hand, try pressing the -pickup- action button to release it.

3. I more than doubled the distance that your real-world hand can move away from the in-game saw while sawing, before it cancels the sawing action. 

Note, I am still working on a fix for the saw failing on a high percentage of cuts.

4. I increased the angle for the hammer to detect a nail head for removal. It should be easier to attach now.

5. I added a cooldown timer for haptics on items to prevent the "run-away" haptics response due to some collision situations.

6. I added a linear displacement, instead of purely a rotational displacement, to the joint of handheld items. You will notice a change to the general dynamics of items in your hand, but the major benefit is that it is harder to push items through objects.

I hope you find these updates helpful, and as always, leave feedback in the Steam Community Forums.

Have fun. Be productive.
